newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Germany gives Zambia $21m, but maintains aid cuts.
newsitem.headline: Germany gives Zambia $21m, but maintains aid cuts.

text.p: Germany has given Zambia $21 million but cut intended aid by more than half because of the "political situation" under President Frederick Chiluba, embassy officials said on Monday.
"Germany has offered the Zambian government $21 million as part of this year's aid allocation," an embassy official told Reuters. "However, the cuts in aid effected this year remain unchanged."
State media said on Monday Germany had lifted its aid squeeze on the Chiluba government after general elections on November 18.
The embassy denied this, with the official saying Germany had initially planned to give Zambia $58 million in 1996.
"In view of the political situation, the German government cut balance of payment support by $20 million. Smaller cuts were made in other areas," he added.

Western governments, led by the United States, froze aid to the southern African country over what they said was a flawed electoral process intended to give Chiluba's Movement for Multiparty Democracy unfair advantage at the polls.
Seven opposition parties, including former president Kenneth Kaunda's United National Independence Party, boycotted the voting that the ruling party won by a landslide.
